title: Finding the early jazz pioneers still alive
summary: Steinau reflects on reading about jazz pioneers as if dead, then discovering many still playing in the late-1940s revival and treating them as patients.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: uh but you know one of the things that that happened that that struck me and i suspect it may have struck you was that what i i i read about jazz before i listened to it i read some go fine i read some panacea uh i read a couple i i guess the 44 and 45 escar jazz books and the way it read i said my goodness all these people must be dead all these legendary pioneers yeah and then when i came back to new orleans out of the army in 1946 and started hearing about people and particularly in the next couple of years years only to find out that an awfully large percentage of them were living many of them playing many of them came out and started playing in the jazz revival it came in the late 40s uh it was it was a constant source of amazement like opening treasure chest after treasure chest and then as i as i as i got on into my later years in medical school in the early 50s and started having some of the musicians and their families as patients uh in my clinical years and talking to some of them about who they had known and what they had done and things like this it was a constant source of fascination i suppose in a way i was in about as ideal a position as a person of my age could have been at the time or pretty close to it to run into things of this sort well it's fantastic to think uh
